lines.en: Why was the Ambassador particularly lucky?
When the Ambassador of Escalopia returned home for lunch, his wife got a shock.
lines.zh: 当埃斯卡洛皮亚大使回家吃午饭时，他的妻子吓了一跳。

lines.en: He looked pale and his clothes were in a frightful state.
lines.zh: 他脸色苍白，衣服也糟透了。

lines.en: 'What has happened?' she asked.
'How did your clothes get into such a mess?'
'A fire extinguisher, my dear,' answered the Ambassador drily.
lines.zh: “灭火器，亲爱的，”大使干巴巴地回答道。

lines.en: 'University students set the Embassy on fire this morning.'
lines.zh: “今天早上大学生把大使馆点着了。”

lines.en: 'Good heavens!' exclaimed his wife.
'And where were you at the time?'
'I was in my office as usual,' answered the Ambassador.
lines.zh: “我像往常一样在办公室里，”大使回答道。

lines.en: 'The fire broke out in the basement.
I went down immediately, of course, and that fool, Horst,
lines.zh: 我当然立刻下去了，然后那个傻瓜霍斯特，

lines.en: aimed a fire extinguisher at me.
He thought I was on fire.
I must definitely get that fellow posted.'
lines.zh: 我一定要把那个家伙调走。”

lines.en: The Ambassador's wife went on asking questions,
when she suddenly noticed a big hole in her husband's hat.
lines.zh: 突然她发现丈夫的帽子上有一个大洞。

lines.en: 'And how can you explain that?' she asked.
'Oh, that,' said the Ambassador.
'Someone fired a shot through my office window.
lines.zh: “有人朝我办公室窗户开了一枪。

lines.en: Accurate, don't you think?
Fortunately, I wasn't wearing it at the time.
If I had been, I would not have been able to get home for lunch.'
lines.zh: 如果我当时戴着，我就不能回家吃午饭了。”
